sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः । निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
hindiTranslation: निद्रा, आलस्य और प्रमादसे उत्पन्न होनेवाला जो सुख आरम्भमें और परिणाममें अपनेको मोहित करनेवाला है, वह सुख तामस कहा गया है ॥
englishTranslation: That pleasure, born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, deludes the self at the beginning and at the end; it is called tamasic.
essence: Pleasure that dulls you is not relief; it is confusion in disguise.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Pleasure that comes from sleep, laziness, and carelessness feels good only briefly. It dulls the mind and leaves a person more confused.
simpleInsight: Not every comfort restores you. Some pleasures quietly drain your clarity.
detailedMeaning: Krishna finishes classifying the three kinds of pleasure. After describing higher and mixed forms, Krishna names the lowest one: the comfort that comes from sleep, laziness, and negligence, and leaves the mind dulled.
modernRelevance: On a holiday, a man sleeps till noon, naps again after lunch and lets the whole day go by. Krishna places that comfort in tamas: it dulls the mind at the start and leaves it duller at the end.
translationLiteral: यत् (which) / अग्रे (at first) / च (and) / अनुबन्धे (in the end) / च (and) / सुखम् (pleasure) / मोहनम् (deluding) / आत्मनः (of the self) / निद्रा-आलस्य-प्रमाद-उत्थम् (born of sleep, laziness, and negligence) / तत् (that) / तामसम् (tamasic) / उदाहृतम् (is called)
insight: Tamasic pleasure, from sleep, sloth and carelessness, deludes the self from start to finish, Krishna says.

quoteVariants.text: Sleep-born pleasure blinds now and later. Tamasic ease is a trap.
If it leaves you dull, it was never real comfort.
Reject the comfort that clouds you.
